changes: All paginated and legacy history turns must explicitly declare full items. A client/thread must complete a continuous traversal before turn or compaction admission, rechecked at the final native write. Creation provenance permits only known unmaterialized first turns.

History traversals are invalidated when a new first page begins, a client or gateway disconnects, or runtime closes. In-flight responses cannot reestablish an old proof. Disconnect releases capacity even if the client has no terminal.

Attachments use per-send in-memory reservation ownership backed by durable thread pins. Only a definitive not_sent releases the current send's uncommitted references; prior pins, overlapping accepted or uncertain references, and restart uncertainty remain retained. A failed rollback is conservative.

Read-only thread/resume no longer accepts options. A known rejected first turn preserves the partial creation receipt without inventing unknown live activity. A genuinely unknown first turn still blocks work.
Observed turn lifecycle or status-only activity invalidates fresh-thread provenance; a later rejected request cannot restore it.
MCP elicitation cancellation, decline, and URL confirmation preserve the official missing/null optional-content semantics. Non-null cancellation content remains invalid.
